scoring.source_summary: The source answer sheet groups question numbers by repeated sequences (1,8,...64; 2,9,...65; etc.), tallies a/b answers, aggregates groups 2+3 for S/N, groups 4+5 for T/F, and groups 6+7 for J/P, then chooses the larger total in each pair. The PDF does not include approved golden test cases.
scoring.production_status: Do not release scoring until exact implementation is validated against an authorised key and approved expected-output cases.
scoring.source_identity_note: The user identifies this module as MBTI, but the PDF itself calls it 'Personality Type Identification Using Psychometric Test' and does not establish that it is the official/licensed Myers-Briggs Type Indicator. Confirm naming, validation and rights with the client before public launch.

assessment_modules.name: Holland Career Interest Inventory (RIASEC)
instructions: Mark the box for each statement that describes you.
Do not base answers on whether you have enough education or training to perform the activity.
Do not base answers on how much money you would make; think about whether you would like or dislike performing the work activity.

statements.text: Able to Think of new ideas

scoring.note: A score is the number of checked statements in that category. This follows the inventory layout and the source interpretation bands. Confirm that each listed statement is intended to count as one point before production.
scoring.source_text_review_required: The fourth Artistic / Are you statement appears as 'Yourself' in the scan. Preserve the literal string but obtain approved corrected text before production. Confirm each checked statement is worth one point.

assessment_modules.name: VARK Learning Styles Questionnaire
instructions: Choose the answer which best explains your preference.
The questionnaire says more than one answer may be selected if a single answer does not match your perception.
Question 15 in the supplied PDF is an instruction: “Ignore question 1.” It is not a question with answer options.

questions.text: How many syllables are in your first name?
You are about to give directions to a person who is standing with you. They are staying in a hotel in town and want to visit your house later. They have a rental car. You would:

options.text: write down the directions (without a map)
collect them from the hotel in my car

questions.text: You are not sure whether a word should be spelled ‘dependent’ or ‘dependant’. I would:

options.text: look it up in the dictionary
see the word in my mind and choose the way it looks
sound it out in my mind
write both versions down on paper and choose one

questions.text: You have just received the latest copy of a magazine with an itinerary for a conference, this is of interest to someone else. You would:

options.text: send them a copy of the printed itinerary
show them on a map of the world

questions.text: You are going to cook something as a special treat for your family. You would:

options.text: cook something familiar without the need for instructions

questions.text: A group of students from another school has been assigned to you to find out about the geology of your local area. You would:

options.text: drive them to a wildlife reserve or park
give them pamphlets or a book on wildlife reserves or parks
give them a talk on wildlife reserves or parks

options.text: the salesperson telling you what you want to know
reading the details about it in a journal

it looks really smart and fashionable

options.text: sit down at the keyboard and begin to experiment with the program features

scoring.method: Count each selected option’s assigned category letter. Multiple selections are permitted by the source, so one response can contribute to multiple category scores.
known_source_gaps: The supplied scoring chart has no scoring assignments for Question 1; keep it unscored as indicated by the chart unless the client supplies an approved key.
The source lists “15. Ignore question 1.” but provides no question or scoring key for Question 15. Do not render this as a question.
